question: What is the primary purpose of indirect nursing care technologies?

options.A: To streamline administrative and logistical workflows away from the bedside
options.B: To diagnose complex medical pathologies without physician intervention
options.C: To replace bedside clinical judgment with automated artificial intelligence
options.D: To monitor patient vital signs continuously via wearable wireless sensors

explanation: These technologies target tasks like inventory management and scheduling, freeing up time for clinical duties. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T5#GNS113_U4_T5_h1)

question: How do indirect care technologies ultimately benefit patient clinical outcomes?

options.A: By reallocating nurse hours from paperwork to direct patient care
options.B: By guaranteeing absolute error-free diagnosis during emergency admissions
options.C: By eliminating the need for routine physician and nursing handovers
options.D: By lowering the overall cost of hospital medications and consumables

explanation: Reducing time spent on logistical burdens allows nurses to focus more energy on actual bedside care. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T5#GNS113_U4_T5_h1)

question: How do active RFID tags differ primarily from passive tags?

options.A: Passive tags are exclusively used for tracking pharmaceutical cold chains
options.B: Passive tags have built-in GPS capabilities for tracking across cities
options.C: Active tags require physical contact with a handheld barcode scanner
options.D: Active tags broadcast signals continuously using an internal power source

explanation: Active tags contain their own transmitters to continuously relay location data without needing a scanner to wake them up. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T5#GNS113_U4_T5_h2)

question: A nurse wastes twenty minutes searching for an infusion pump during a critical medication round. Which technology would best prevent this delay in the future?
explanation: RFID systems map the physical location of portable hospital equipment in real time. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T5#GNS113_U4_T5_h2)

question: What is a major advantage of electronic inventory systems over manual ledger books?

options.A: Automatic manufacture of pharmaceuticals within the hospital
options.B: Real-time tracking of stock deductions as items are used
options.C: Elimination of the need for any physical storage spaces
options.D: Prevention of all expiration dates through chemical stabilization

explanation: Digital systems update inventory counts instantly upon usage, avoiding delayed manual tallies. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T5#GNS113_U4_T5_h3)

question: Which scenario indicates an electronic inventory system is successfully fulfilling its purpose on a surgical ward?

options.A: Nurses spend extra hours each evening counting remaining bandages
options.B: Expired medications are discovered months after their shelf life ends
options.C: An automated purchase order is generated before sterile gauze runs out
options.D: The ward accumulates surplus stock to hide poor usage metrics

explanation: Pre-set reorder thresholds trigger restocking automatically to avert stockouts. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T5#GNS113_U4_T5_h3)

question: What core variable do computerized staffing systems use to determine shift requirements?

options.A: Proximity of staff residences to work

explanation: Rostering algorithms base staffing needs on how sick the patients are and how many occupy the ward. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T5#GNS113_U4_T5_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical benefit of implementing a computerized rostering system?

options.A: Reducing the administrative hours spent manually drafting schedules
options.B: Eliminating the need for any clinical handovers between shifts
options.C: Maintaining safe, compliant nurse-to-patient ratios across wards
options.D: Allowing transparent digital shift swaps among nursing colleagues

explanation: Rostering software manages schedules and staffing levels, but clinical handovers remain essential for safe patient care continuity. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T5#GNS113_U4_T5_h4)

question: What is a major infrastructure challenge when deploying health technologies in many developing clinical settings?

options.A: Instantaneous hardware obsolescence occurring every week
options.B: Unstable power supplies and intermittent internet access
options.C: Excessive bandwidth speeds that overload local servers
options.D: An absolute surplus of trained biomedical software engineers

explanation: Unreliable power and connectivity pose significant hurdles requiring offline backups and generators. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T5#GNS113_U4_T5_h5)

question: Why can poorly integrated indirect technologies inadvertently increase nurse burnout?

options.A: By forcing staff to perform redundant manual and digital data entry
options.B: By automatically assigning nurses to night shifts without warning
options.C: By completely removing all administrative tasks from the hospital
options.D: By shortening shift lengths beyond what is legally permissible

explanation: If systems do not talk to each other, nurses end up typing the same information into multiple places. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T5#GNS113_U4_T5_h5)

question: Which factor is critical when designing future nursing informatics tools to ensure high uptake?

options.A: Removing all data security and privacy protocols to speed access
options.B: Restricting system access exclusively to senior hospital directors
options.C: Ensuring the software requires no electricity or battery backups
options.D: Active involvement of nurses in reflecting real clinical workflows

explanation: Tools designed with frontline nurse input match clinical realities much better than top-down administrative software. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T5#GNS113_U4_T5_h6)

question: What does system 'interoperability' mean in the context of hospital informatics?

options.A: Every department using a completely separate, isolated software
options.B: Different digital platforms sharing and exchanging data seamlessly
options.C: Manual paper records serving as the ultimate legal backup
options.D: Staff members rotating through various wards every single month

explanation: Interoperability allows inventory, staffing, and electronic health records to communicate without friction. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T5#GNS113_U4_T5_h6)
